messages:
maria: Heads up — dedicated eu2 is showing a p95/p99 burst pattern for embeddings and realtime routes after the capacity switchover. Customers (Acme, Nebula) reporting 10–30s tail latencies.
support-ops: Raised tickets with both customers and asked for sample request_ids. keeping them updated.
deploy-bot: Rollout started: kernel+driver batch -> kernel 6.1.x + nvidia-driver 525.16 to pool dedicated-eu2 at 22:43 UTC. (staged) :information_source:
raj: seeing the same. spike aligns with the driver+kernel push. NVMe queue depth looks noisy on a subset of nodes. suspect host-storage contention interacting with driver i/o paths.
lucas: oncall — grabbing metrics and logs now. can someone paste a quick dmesg/iostat snippet from an affected node?
maria: attaching a tiny excerpt from node-221 (trimmed):
```
[ 127834.345678] nvme0: I/O 91234 QID 0 timeout, 5000ms
[ 127834.346001] nvme0: controller reset recovery failed
[ 127834.346512] NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x86)
[ 127834.347000] audit: type=1400 audit(127834.34:123): apparmor="DENIED" ...
```
(more lines show repeated nvme timeouts, nvme controller resets).
elaine: kv-cache hit rate is steady, so model caching doesn't look like the cause. this reads like hostfs/NVMe stalls causing the GPU driver to block on underlying io; requests queue up and p99 balloons.
raj: agree. quick mitigation options: 1) route live traffic for heavy embedding customers to fallback pool (dedicated-eu2-fallback) 2) drain nodes showing NVMe controller resets 3) rollback to driver 524.* if rollout correlated 4) ask infra to check NVMe firmware and cloud provider for SMART/telemetry.
maria: doing 1 + 2 now — starting cordon/drain on node-221 and node-223. routing rule flipped for Acme. marking incident P1.
support-ops: Noted — customers bumped to fallback pool, reporting reduced errors so far (waiting on latency numbers).
lucas: running the bisect script to find which image in the rollout coincides with NVMe errors. also collecting sar/iostat/perf/trace-cmd on the drained nodes. will upload artifacts to the incident.
raj: if rollback is needed, we should coordinate a canary rollback for a small subset first. also suggest temporarily lowering per-request batch_size and concurrent streams on the dedicated serving gateway to reduce IO pressure.
deploy-bot: Canaries: 12/120 nodes reverted to driver 524.99 at 22:57 UTC (in progress).
maria: initial numbers after routing flip: p95 dropped from ~2.3s -> 600ms, p99 reduced but still elevated. some requests still hit 5–8s. taking logs and traces.
elainE: typo: spelled my name wrong? (small laugh) — confirming: if nvme resets persist post-rollback, escalate to hardware/cloud vendor. also check nvme firmware versions across nodes: we saw mixed firmware in this pool.
raj: +1. next steps: 1) finish rollback canary, 2) if stable, roll forward rollback to remaining nodes, 3) if not stable, open vendor support with SMART/telemetry and full dmesg stacks.
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-20260317-1745 (dedicated-eu2 p99 storage/driver interaction).
lucas: collected traces uploaded: s3://redwood-incidents/INC-20260317-1745/artifacts.tar.gz — includes iostat, dmesg, nvme-cli output, perf stats.
maria: if rollback finishes and tail latencies drop to baseline within 15m we close P1. if not, escalate to vendor immediately. will post updates. :thumbsup:
